sentences.label: Plans
sentences.text: These add up independently: through this sum alone, an international plan takes a typical customer's chance of leaving from about 2% to about 24%, a voice-mail plan lowers it to under 1%, and more voice-mail messages raise it steadily, from about 2% at 0 to about 6% at 32 messages; all three also act through the parts below.

sentences.label: Usage
sentences.text: More international minutes (through this sum alone, about 1% at 7 to about 4% at 14 minutes; they also act through the total bill, below), more evening minutes (about 2% at 138 to about 3% at 266 minutes), a higher night-time charge (about 2% at 6.13 to about 3% at 11.88 US dollars) and a longer account (about 2% at 48 to about 3% at 152) raise it steadily.

sentences.label: State
sentences.text: Through this sum alone, the state shifts it up or down: from about 2% in West Virginia to about 9% in California, about 7% in Washington and about 5% in New Jersey, and down to under 1% in Vermont and about 1% in Alaska and Wyoming (each of these states has 41 to 90 training customers; the state also acts through the parts below, and the full list is in the technical detail).

sentences.label: Barely or not at all
sentences.text: The area code barely changes it, and the model ignores daytime calls, international calls, the international charge, night-time calls and night-time minutes.

This part combines customer-service calls, the daytime charge, the international plan and the state, and acts on 1303 of 4000 training customers, 302 of whom left; for the typical customer it acts on, the chance of leaving is about 2% without it and about 3% with it.

Through it, customer-service calls add to the chance only from about 3 calls (between 1 and 3 calls for different customers) upwards, in an uneven way: for a typical customer, going from 0 to 4 calls takes it from about 2% to about 13%.
The calls count more for customers with a daytime charge of 30.69 US dollars or less, rising slowly at first, then faster, from about 2% to about 6% at 3 calls, against about 2% for those above it.

A higher daytime charge lowers the chance through it, steadily up to about 15.64 US dollars (between 7.93 and 31.04 US dollars for different customers), then no further: for the typical customer it acts on, from about 11% at 19.07 to about 2% at 42.40 US dollars.

parts.original_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS (revised): rare-state units that are almost inert. 14 hidden nodes driven only by state one-hots (states 50, 23, 22, 1, 28, 32, 44, 12, 2; ~55-105 rows each, large z-values) plus a tiny vmail-messages term. The cascade 3854->13212->8290->948->{13939,11368}->14533->1887 is on for <=105 rows and reaches the output through weights -0.09 then -0.015: zero measurable effect. 1887 (state:28) moves the logit by at most -0.23; 7740 (state:44, always on via bias) by at most +0.40 on state:44 rows; 4332 (state:12) +0.07; 15985 (state:2) +0.02; 3854 (state:32/44) feeds the relay with activation <=0.08. EVIDENCE: closed form (max err 0.022, sympy rounding through the deep cascade); sensitivities all <0.04 except 7740/state:44 (0.98 per unit of activation but output weight 0.05). Mean-ablating the whole leaf changes train AUC by -0.0002; its best linear fit has R2 1.000. The large per-state effects in this network are in the root's direct linear edges, not here.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients

ann_79.text: This part acts on 1033 of 4000 training customers (26%); nearly all of them are customers without a voice-mail plan.
For a typical customer it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted chance that a customer leaves from about 2% without this part to about 6% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 283 of these 1033 customers had churn.
